title: Cut involuntary churn from failed card payments
statement: Ledgerline customers on monthly plans churn when their card payment fails and nobody notices. Today a failed charge sends one email and then the account is suspended after 7 days. We want to recover most of these customers automatically: retry intelligently, tell the customer clearly what happened and how to fix it, and give our support team visibility into who is at risk before the suspension hits. This is the single largest controllable source of revenue loss this year.

success_metrics.target: Below 2.9% within two months of launch
success_metrics.measurement: Monthly cohort report in Metabase, dashboard 'Billing health'

success_metrics.baseline: 38% of failed charges recovered within 7 days
success_metrics.measurement: payments.recovered_at within 7 days of first failure

success_metrics.target: Support can list at-risk accounts and see retry history without engineering help

must_not: No change to the pricing or plan catalogue
No new third-party payment provider; stay on Stripe
No destructive schema migrations on the payments table
compliance: PCI: never store raw card data; use Stripe tokens only

context_links.note: Rails monolith; billing lives under app/services/billing
Current dunning behaviour, written by support

clarifications.question: Should retries follow Stripe Smart Retries or our own schedule?
clarifications.answer: Use Stripe Smart Retries as the engine; we own the customer messaging and the admin view.
